title: [Proposal] Contract Evaluation Agent Template
description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: aden-hive/hive. Labels: enhancement, help wanted, good first issue, size: large. # [Proposal] Contract Evaluation Agent Template

## Summary
Proposing a new agent template for automated NDA analysis that demonstrates Hive's multi-node architecture, human-in-the-loop intervention, and production-oriented workflows.

## Motivation
Legal contract review is time-consuming (15-30 min per NDA) and expensive. An AI agent could automate initial screening, flag problematic clauses, and escalate complex cases to human reviewers.

This addresses:
- The call for example agents in the README
- Need for production-ready templates (not toy demos)
- Demonstrating Hive's advanced capabilities in a real business domain

## Proposed Agent

### Scope
**Initial focus: NDAs only** (manageable validation scope)
- Document processing (PDF/DOCX)
- Clause detection (confidentiality, liability, terms, obligations)
- Mutual vs one-sided analysis
- Risk scoring with human escalation
- Structured report generation

### Architecture
Multi-node workflow:
1. Document ingestion
2. Classification
3. Parallel analysis nodes (confidentiality, liability, terms, dates)
4. Human-in-the-loop review (if risk ≥ threshold)
5. Report generation

### Validation Plan
- 20+ publicly available NDAs with ground truth
- Measurable metrics: precision, recall, processing time, cost
- Reproducible test suite
- Document known limitations and failure cases

## Value Proposition
- Demonstrates complex Hive workflows (parallel nodes, HITL, structured LLM outputs)
- Real business application with measurable validation
- Template for similar specialized agents
- Open-source alternative to expensive legal tech

## Implementation Status
**Concept stage** - seeking feedback before implementation:
- Proposed architecture and validation methodology documented
- Ready to build once scope/approach is approved

title: feat(core): SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria rule pack (third framework)
description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: Opencomplai/opencomplai. Labels: enhancement, help wanted. ## Context
Third framework pack on the same pluggable architecture (see #64 ISO/IEC 27001 and #65 NIST AI RMF). SOC 2 readiness is a well-understood, near-term compliance target for AI/SaaS vendors, and mapping Trust Services Criteria (Security, Availability, Confidentiality, Processing Integrity, Privacy) is a well-documented control set to encode.

## Proposal
Add a SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria control-mapping pack, scoped the same way as the ISO 27001 pack: evidence-assembly and gap-reporting, not a certification claim.

## Why this is complex
SOC 2 criteria are organized very differently from both EU AI Act risk tiers and NIST's four functions (criteria + points of focus, largely process/organizational rather than model-behavior controls) — a third distinct shape is a strong test of whether the framework abstraction holds up, and surfaces which parts of `control_catalog.py` are still EU-AI-Act-shaped.

## Acceptance criteria
- SOC 2 TSC mapped onto the framework's `Control` model
- Golden-vector tests
- Documented in `docs/src/concepts/` alongside the existing Annex IV coverage docs

title: Publish capability: core.consent-purpose-check (consent / purpose binding check)
description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: traverse-framework/registry. Labels: enhancement, good first issue, help wanted, no-spec-needed. ## Why

Agents that process personal data need a **purpose-binding check**: given recorded consents and a requested processing purpose, is the action allowed? This is business/governance logic, not a string util — capability decides, agent does not invent legal conclusions.

## One-PR ask

Publish **`core.consent-purpose-check@1.0.0`**:

**Inputs:**
- `subject_id`: string
- `requested_purpose`: string (from a closed enum or caller-supplied catalog ids)
- `consents`: array of `{ "purpose": string, "status": "granted"|"denied"|"withdrawn", "granted_at"?: string (ISO-8601), "expires_at"?: string | null, "scope"?: string[] }`
- `now`: string (ISO-8601) — caller-supplied clock (pure; no ambient time)
- `policy_version`: string

**Outputs:**
- `decision`: `allow` | `deny`
- `reason_code`: e.g. `consent_granted` | `consent_withdrawn` | `consent_expired` | `purpose_not_granted` | `invalid_input`
- `matched_consent_index`: integer | null
- `policy_version`: string

**Behavior:** Exact purpose match (document whether scope must also intersect). Withdrawn/expired/denied → deny. No consent row → deny (fail closed). Invalid timestamps → fail closed.

Follow [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/traverse-framework/registry/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and [`capabilities/README.md`](https://github.com/traverse-framework/registry/blob/main/capabilities/README.md) publish checklist.

title: Add industry file: Legal Tech
description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: glacierphonk/naming. Labels: enhancement, help wanted, good first issue, industry. ## Task

Add a legal tech naming guide at \`industries/legaltech.md\`. Depends on #180.

## Why legal tech naming is distinct

- **Authority and gravitas required** — lawyers are conservative buyers. Playful names feel unserious
- **Latin legal vocabulary** — massive untapped naming source (habeas, certiorari, amicus, pro bono — but also pretentious if misused)
- **Trust + precision** — legal products handle sensitive documents, contracts, privileged communications
- **Regulated profession** — \"attorney\" and \"lawyer\" have legal meaning. Names that imply legal advice when the product doesn't provide it are risky
- **Old industry meets new tech** — naming must bridge tradition and innovation

## Sections to cover

- Case studies: Harvey (AI), Clio, Ironclad, Everlaw, LegalZoom, Rocket Lawyer
- Anti-patterns: \"Legal[X]\", \"[X]Law\", fake Latin, over-gravitas
- Territory map: Shield/protection, compass/guidance, ledger/record, bridge/arbitration

## Before submitting

Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and run \`markdownlint-cli2 '**/*.md'\` before pushing.

title: test: add tests for gdpr_compliance.rego (GDPR)
description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: ynotbhatc/rego_policy_libraries. Labels: help wanted, good first issue. **File:** `frameworks/privacy/gdpr/gdpr_compliance.rego` (292 lines)
**Package:** `gdpr.compliance`
**Standard:** GDPR

This policy uses **boolean rules**: `default <name> := false` with a matching
`<name> if { ... }`. There are roughly **21** of them.

For each, write a case with input that makes it true, and one where it stays
false. Boolean rules are where the `{}` trap bites — a rule with no `default`
is *undefined* rather than false, and one undefined field collapses the whole
report object.

### Done when

- [ ] `opa test frameworks/privacy/gdpr -v` passes
- [ ] Each rule has a case that exercises it
- [ ] At least one case asserts nothing fires on compliant input
- [ ] The compliance report is asserted to be a **populated object on empty input**, not `{}`

### Where to put it

`frameworks/privacy/gdpr/tests/test_gdpr_compliance.rego`, package `gdpr.compliance_test`.

The pattern to copy, and the `array.concat` trap, are in
[CONTRIBUTING.md](../blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). The full queue of untested
policies is in [COVERAGE.md](../blob/main/COVERAGE.md).

---

*Comment before you start so two people don't write the same test.*

title: Suggestion: Word Add-In and DOCX Editing Feature — AI-Powered Document Redlining with Live Tracked Changes
description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: LegalQuants/lq-ai. Labels: enhancement, help wanted. ## Feature Suggestion: Word Add-In & DOCX Editing

This issue proposes a **Chat & Edit Legal Docx** feature — AI-powered document editing with live redlines, designed as both a web editor and MS Word Add-In.

### What This Is

A Vault + Document Editor chat surface where lawyers can:
- Upload matter bundles and chat with AI about documents
- Draft new documents or propose redlines against precedent
- Review AI-generated edits as **live tracked changes** (Word native or web redlines)
- Confirm writes before any mutation (human-in-the-loop)
- Export clean DOCX without compromising privilege

title: soup loop canary writes three fields to loop.yaml and nothing reads them: no traffic split, no canary verdict, no rollback — and the pre-wired deploy records verdict "OK" on a 200
description:
